exercises.prompt: Identify the mood and inflectional sign of يَفْهَمَ in the sentence below.
exercises.explanation: The purpose particle كَيْ governs the following imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood (manṣūb), marked by final fatḥah on sound singular stems.

feedback.rule: Subjunctive governing particles (ḥurūf al-naṣb) change final -u to -a on singular sound stems.
feedback.role: Imperfect verb in subordinate purpose clause
feedback.commonError: Do not mistake the fatḥah on a verb for accusative case—verbs take moods (rafʿ, naṣb, jazm), not nominal cases.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct subjunctive form after لَنْ for the 3rd person masculine plural ('They will never return').
exercises.explanation: يَرْجِعُونَ belongs to al-afʿāl al-khamsah; in the subjunctive after لَنْ, final nūn is dropped (ḥadhf al-nūn) and alif al-fāriqah is written: يَرْجِعُوا.

feedback.rule: Al-afʿāl al-khamsah mark the subjunctive by dropping final nūn (ḥadhf al-nūn).
feedback.governor: لَنْ (particle of emphatic future negation and naṣb)
feedback.commonError: Retaining final nūn (يَرْجِعُونَ) leaves the verb in the indicative.

exercises.prompt: True or False: Both أَنْ and أَنَّ govern imperfect verbs in the subjunctive mood.
exercises.explanation: False. أَنْ (with sukūn) governs imperfect verbs in the subjunctive, whereas أَنَّ (with shaddah) belongs to the sisters of إِنَّ and governs nominal clauses.

feedback.rule: Distinguish verbal subjunctive particle أَنْ from nominal corroborating particle أَنَّ.
feedback.commonError: Confusing أَنْ + verb with أَنَّ + noun/pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the tokens to form: 'I want to write the letter.'
exercises.explanation: The main indicative verb أُرِيدُ precedes the subjunctive particle أَنْ, which governs أَكْتُبَ, followed by the accusative object الرِّسَالَةَ.

feedback.rule: Main verb + أَنْ + subjunctive verb + direct object.
